- News coverage by country: India 95 articles of 148 in the top rows (64.2%), the United States 31, Bangladesh 4 [c1]. Shares are of the top rows only [c1].
- the health literature index first-author affiliation: United States 15, China 9, India 3 [c1]. This measures only 7 the health literature index records and does not represent the Indian literature.
- Institutions by lift over their corpus share: Geological Survey of India (85 papers), IIT Roorkee (181), National Institute of Hydrology (56) [c1].
- Sub-regions: north and northwest India, the Ganges basin and the Hindon basin dominate the key numbers [c1]. The tool gives no state-level breakdown.

## Evidence
- [r1] Mishra et al., 2024, Earth's Future, article tier. Supports the 450 km³ loss and the 1.5 cm/year rate. Quote: "rapid groundwater depletion (∼1.5 cm/year) in north India with a net loss of 450 km 3 of groundwater during 2002–2021."
- [r2] Panda et al., 2020, Hydrological Processes, article. Quote: "increased rapidly from 17 km 3 to 189 km 3 between the pre‑2002 and 2002–2013 periods."
- [r3] Mishra et al., 2018, Earth's Future, article. Quote: "in the range of 122 to 199 billion m 3."
- [r4] Joshi et al., 2021, Journal of Hydrology, article. Supports the heterogeneity of NW India.
- [r5] Mukherjee et al., 2018, Scientific Reports, article. Supports the baseflow link to Ganges summer drying.
- [r6] Jadav & Yadav, 2025, Journal of Hydrology Regional Studies, article. Supports station-level declines.
- [r7] Maina et al., 2024, Communications Earth & Environment, article. Irrigation-driven depletion reduces streamflow to the Bay of Bengal (title-level claim only).
- [r8] Bhattarai et al., 2021, Environmental Research Letters, article. Title: "The impact of groundwater depletion on agricultural production in India". Findings not extracted.

All are article tier with "moderate" strength [c1]. No review-tier evidence was found [c1].

## Method and limits
- Windows: research 2017–2025; the gap to today (2026-10-23) is about 10 months. News ends 2026-06-01, a gap of about 4.7 months. The newest news months are censored because ingest lags [c2].
- Lanes: all subject lane [c1]. Match mode for news is "mention" [c2], so counts include passing mentions.
- Coverage: research arrives as 1,580 typed papers but only 22 with readable abstracts, and key numbers come from a handful of them. the health literature index has 7 records, so its geography is not representative [c1].
- Counts measure papers and articles that match the term, not the severity of depletion.
- Cannot answer: state-level depletion rates, the share attributable to irrigation versus climate, a post-2021 well-level trend, or economic loss. The tool returned no review-tier consensus.
- The 2025-03 critical-share dip (44.4%) is unexplained [c2]. The reading of the "contested" mix is my interpretation.
- The brief lists a California Central Valley paper among its sources, which is not about India.
